FM14.reasoning: The agent trains and evaluates stochastic models (LightGBM, CatBoost) exactly once on a single validation split, without using cross-validation or averaging over multiple random seeds.

FM15.reasoning: The agent uses only accuracy as the evaluation metric, which is not robust for evaluating performance on tasks with imbalanced classes like readmission predicting.

FM07.reasoning: The agent uses the raw columns as-is, applying only basic missing value imputation and categorical encoding, completely lacking any domain-specific feature engineering.

other_failure_modes.name: Discarded Original IDs in Submission
other_failure_modes.description: The agent drops the original identifier columns from the test set during data cleaning and generates an artificial sequence of integers for the submission file. This will cause the predictions to be misaligned or rejected by any downstream evaluation system that expects predictions mapped to the original IDs.

summary: The agent creates a functional machine learning pipeline with proper train/validation splitting, but it fails to account for patient-level grouping, leading to subject overlap leakage. It evaluates models only once using accuracy, ignores feature engineering, and crucially replaces the original test IDs with an arbitrary sequence, which will break the final submission.
